title: BlueCrest co-sell opportunity gating and ops handshake
summary: Initial co-sell gating and operational handshake for BlueCrest deal. Covered qualification, target SLAs, required security docs, pilot scope, routing/fallback strategy, and next-step commitments for an executive sponsor intro and a pilot kickoff week. Some transcription errors present (product names, acronyms).
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored pricing + pilot SOW by 2026-05-25
BlueCrest to confirm exec sponsor and procurement timeline by 2026-05-22
Evan to run internal perf estimate and share expected token cost by 2026-05-24

Maya Chen - Draft pilot SOW + pricing and send to James and Rita by 2026-05-25

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~59 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Lina (CSM), James (BlueCrest), Rita (BlueCrest procurement), Samir (BlueCrest platform), Olivia (sales ops)

Summary (auto): Quick gating call to align on co-sell mechanics, pilot scope, security checklist, and who owns the handoffs. Decks referenced: https://redwood.ai/decks/bluecrest-co-sell (shared), security pack link (sent post-call).

00:00:10 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, um do folks have the agenda?
00:00:22 James: yeah thanks, uh James here, head of partnerships at BlueCrest. We just want to make sure the pilot and co-sell ops don't hit surprises — procurement's watching timeline closely.
00:00:35 Maya: totally. quick intro from our side — Evan's gonna run through perf and ops considerations, Lina on enablement and success.
00:00:44 Evan: hi all, Evan Torres, platform solutions. we'll cover routing, KV cache behavior, and what Dedicated vs hosted looks like. bear with me if i stumble on product names — sometimes the auto transcript mangles "Redwood Dedicatedy" lol.

00:01:10 Rita: procurement here, timeline is tight — legal needs to see encryption details, SOC2 cert, and KMS integrations. also pricing bands matter.
00:01:22 Maya: understood — we'll attach SOC2 and ISO certs and a KMS integration note. quick question James — what's the top metric that makes this a green deal for you?
00:01:34 James: two things: 1) throughput — need predictable latency under 200 ms p95 for our checkout microflow; 2) cost curve — can't exceed our per-session budget. also we need to present a pilot ROI for the board.

00:02:05 Evan: ok for 200ms p95 that's aggressive, depends on model and sequence length. we can route to a low-latency variant in Redwood Dedicated or a trimmed quantized variant in hosted. tradeoffs: Dedicated gives consistent latency, hosted is cheaper but fluctuates.
00:02:35 Samir: can you explain the routing and fallback? our infra sometimes has bursty traffic during promos.
00:02:44 Evan: sure — policy-based routing: primary is Dedicated in us-west, fallback to hosted or a smaller quantized model if capacity is constrained. prefix/KV cache helps for repeated prompts; that reduces cost and latency if your patterns are cache-friendly. sometimes the transcript shows KV as "K V" cache which is weird.

00:03:20 Olivia: how does region/residency work? we need EU data residency for EU customers.
00:03:28 Maya: we support region pinning — you can route EU traffic to eu-west with the private control plane. for pilot we can do us-west only then expand.

00:04:05 James: procurement — any special IP or logging audit we should know?
00:04:12 Lina: audit logs are available at token-level granularity in the console, retention choices are configurable as an add-on. we'll include a sample log export.

00:06:00 Rita: security-wise we need to verify SSO/SAML and RBAC before pilot start. also encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is a must.
00:06:12 Evan: KMS/HSM integration is supported; customer-managed key options exist in our private deployment. for hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK via our KMS partner — will share the KMS note.

00:07:05 James: can we do a short technical walkthrough of what the pilot topology looks like? Samir's gonna be the main technical contact.
00:07:12 Evan: yeah quick sketch: 1) API layer in BlueCrest app talks to Redwood routing endpoint over mTLS; 2) requests for the pilot go to a pinned Dedicated tenant; 3) fallback path to hosted if Dedicated is saturated; 4) metrics/trace ingestion into BlueCrest's Datadog. we'll send an architecture diagram.

00:08:30 Samir: on peering — we currently run in an AWS VPC with strict egress policies. can you do VPC peering or private link?
00:08:40 Evan: both options. VPC peering or PrivateLink (we call it private connector) are possible. for on-prem we also have a package but that needs longer lead time. we'll note constraints and required firewall rules.

00:09:55 James: what's the recommended model for cost optimization? quantization? batching?
00:10:02 Evan: a few levers: 1) quantized model variants trade a bit of quality for cost savings; 2) continuous batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU cost but may add tail latency — we can set latency SLOs to small windows to keep p95 under your target; 3) prefix/KV caching helps for repeated cart prompts. we'll run numbers for your workload shape (50 req/s sustained, spikes to 200 req/s during promos).

00:11:30 Olivia: would love a spreadsheet with cost scenarios so sales ops can plug into our models.
00:11:36 Maya: yes we'll attach a cost calc (example sheet) and Evan will populate the BlueCrest-specific row.

00:13:05 James: on co-sell motion — are there joint collateral and lead routing expectations? we have a channel rep who needs to know commission and lead assignment.

00:13:18 Lina: we typically do a partner playbook for co-sell: joint logos, co-branded pitch deck, lead escalation path, and a simple MQA routing doc. we'll propose a one-pager and a folder in the partner portal.

00:14:05 Rita: contract terms — is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated? and what does the pilot commit look like?
00:14:14 Maya: Dedicated often has a reserved capacity commit; pilot can be a time-boxed usage SOW with a credit against future committed spend if you convert to Dedicated. we'll put options in the SOW draft.

00:16:40 James: risk items — what keeps this from going sideways? latency misses, model regressions, or security blockers?
00:16:50 Evan: yep those three. to mitigate: 1) we'll run a pre-pilot perf run against a replay of your traffic (Samir to provide sample traces); 2) Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization/profile settings; 3) dedicated rollbacks and automatic fallback policy to keep the app online if a new model misbehaves.

00:18:00 Samir: about the replay — what's the format and how to scrub PII?
00:18:08 Evan: JSONL with masked fields works. we have a small tool to anonymize tokens — will share instructions and a scrub checklist.

00:20:45 James: what does success look like at the end of the pilot?
00:20:51 Lina: defined by three KPIs: 1) latency p95 under 200ms in production-like load; 2) per-session cost below $X (we'll define exact number in SOW); 3) business metric lift (conversion % uplift) measured A/B with 2 weeks of traffic.

00:23:10 Rita: procurement timeline — we need SOW + security pack for legal review; can this happen this week?
00:23:18 Maya: we'll target to send SOW and price by 2026-05-25, security pack by EOD tomorrow.

00:25:00 Olivia: for co-sell, who is our joint point of contact at Redwood for opportunity updates?
00:25:06 Maya: that'll be Maya for commercial, Evan for technical, Lina for post-sale success. we'll loop in a partner ops contact later.

00:27:45 James: quick question on metrics — can we get token-level cost breakdowns and traces per route?
00:27:53 Evan: yes, the console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and per model. we can also stream traces to Datadog.

00:29:00 Samir: any limitations on model customizations or fine-tuning? we do some domain-specific prompts and might want a small fine-tune.
00:29:09 Evan: fine-tuning support exists but is different across variants; for pilot, prompt engineering + few-shot tends to be quicker. fine-tune or retrieval-augmented generation can be discussed for phase two.

00:31:20 James: competitor watch — we've also been talking to RivalAI and CloudServe ML, their pitch is cheaper at scale. why choose Redwood?
00:31:29 Maya: quick differentiators: production-first runtime with predictable economics, unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private, and immediate co-sell support with partner ops. we'll share customer references.

00:33:00 Rita: legal will want liability and data handling clarified. any standard exclusions?
00:33:08 Maya: standard software SAAS terms — we'll include a data handling addendum. for plate security items we'll send a redline-friendly SOW.

00:35:40 James: ok — let's walk through the pilot week plan.
00:35:45 Evan: proposed: Week 0: architecture signoff and firewall rules; Week 1: perf replay + baseline run; Week 2: small public pilot (limited traffic) with metrics collection; Week 3: ramp and finalize co-sell materials. target production-like tests by end of week 3.

00:37:22 Samir: that seems tight but doable if we get firewall rules and sample traces. I'll aim to deliver those by 2026-05-23.

00:39:10 Maya: note — for the co-sell pitch we should have an exec brief for your VP Sales. James, can you intro us?
00:39:16 James: yes i'll intro to VP Sales (Sara Mills) after i confirm sponsor.

00:40:00 Olivia: for lead routing, we use Salesforce — how do you want to receive leads and how are credits assigned?
00:40:08 Lina: we'll provide a partner lead form and an MQA (marketing qualified account) flow. for credits we can define a co-sell ruleset in the partner playbook.

00:42:50 Rita: one last procurement nit — invoice timing and payment terms?
00:42:57 Maya: standard is net30 for pilots, for committed Dedicated deals we can negotiate net60 or milestone-based invoicing. we'll note that in the SOW.

00:45:20 Evan: i'll remind the team to include a perf baseline and a contingency plan in the SOW (fallback rules, model pinning).

00:47:00 James: anything else from the BlueCrest side?
00:47:05 Rita: no, just need the security pack and SOW asap.

00:49:30 Maya: recap of next steps: 1) Evan provides perf/cost numbers; 2) Maya drafts SOW + pricing; 3) security pack delivered tomorrow; 4) Samir shares traces/firewall by 5/23; 5) James confirms exec sponsor by 5/22.

00:51:00 James: thanks everyone. will wait for the doc bundle and we'll triage internally.
00:51:12 Olivia: thanks all.
00:51:18 Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for kickoff week once SOW is accepted.

00:58:40 system: call ended

Notes: shared artifacts referenced — partner deck (link above), security pack (to be attached), cost calc spreadsheet (internal). Some speaker labels may be off; transcript has occasional auto-caption errors (e.g., "Redwood Dedicatedy", "K V cache").
